methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Arc Boats is a Series B-stage transportation company founded by Mitch Lee and Ryan Cook, having raised $100M+ to date. The private transportation sector contains seven identified comparable companies, including Rivian, The Boring Company, and Einride, though none qualify as direct valuation peers due to stage, timing, or valuation-tier mismatches.

A single applicable valuation method was deployed: stage-progression analysis. Using the $100M total raised as a baseline proxy for current valuation, a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to later growth stages yields $190M. This multiplier reflects observed financing patterns in the sector for companies transitioning from early-to-mid stage to late-stage rounds.

The peer-median approach was not applicable; while three same-sector peers exist in the Transportation universe, none met minimum thresholds of three companies clustering at the same financing stage, adjacent stage, or comparable valuation tier. Applying an all-sector median would lack precision given Arc Boats' specific sub-vertical and capital intensity.

The triangulated valuation range is $162M (low) to $218M (high), with a median of $190M. This range carries meaningful uncertainty: the single-method foundation constrains confidence, and the absence of tightly clustered transaction comparables limits precision. Key risks include the validity of stage-progression multiples in frontier transportation sub-verticals and potential divergence of Arc Boats' capital efficiency from sector norms.
